aggregation: For each criterion, award zero=0, partial=0.5 or full=1 to every listed unit. Multiply the mean of its unit levels by its maximum. Add unrounded criterion points, then round the total to two decimals. All units and all five native case runs must resolve; evaluator failures never count as zero. Latest valid completed submission per participant ranks; a pending replacement suspends the previous rank. Equal totals share competition rank (1,1,3).
notScored: Length, command names, agent count, file existence, generic advice or self-improvement claims
Additional supporting files or helper scripts merely being present
failureRule: Participant omissions in an otherwise completed case are assessed against the criterion examples. Missing runtime inputs, timeouts, malformed grader output, unsupported grader citations or unresolved qualitative disagreement require attention and prevent a final score. Never invent a participant failure to complete a result.

criteria.title: Detects actual defects
criteria.practice: Compare the change with explicit requirements.
criteria.input: Actual reviews of the server, UI and changed-path cases.
criteria.automatic: Match required units and validate cited excerpts.
criteria.judgment: Does the finding identify the actual broken behavior and its cause?

examples.zero: Misses the retry defect or names an unrelated issue.
examples.partial: Identifies the wrong retry response but does not explain the duplicate request condition.
examples.full: Explains that a reused retry receives 202 instead of 200, citing the handler and requirement.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

criteria.title: Avoids unsupported findings on correct changes
criteria.practice: Verify a concern before reporting a defect.
criteria.automatic: Check that the complete output is retained.
criteria.judgment: Are reported defects supported? Does the review distinguish limitations from failures?

examples.zero: Declares the correct retry mapping broken, or supplies no review.
examples.partial: Avoids a false defect but gives only a vague pass without explaining what was checked.
examples.full: Explains the correct behavior with evidence and makes no unsupported defect claim.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

criteria.title: Uses accurate, checkable evidence
criteria.practice: Inspect sources and connect evidence to claims.
criteria.input: Decisive claims and citations in every case output.
criteria.automatic: Validate source paths, lines and exact excerpts in grader judgments.
criteria.judgment: Do the participant references and reasoning support the claim? A real line alone is insufficient.

examples.zero: Invents test execution or supplies no checkable support.
examples.partial: Uses a relevant source but a decisive claim lacks a clear supporting location or explanation.
examples.full: Connects decisive claims to the supplied source or check record, with accurate locations and an explanation of what it proves.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

criteria.title: Handles missing or conflicting evidence honestly
criteria.input: Review with an absent result and a check from a different revision.
criteria.automatic: Check complete input and output records.
criteria.judgment: Does the review identify both the missing check and stale/conflicting evidence without inventing a result?

examples.zero: Claims the submitted revision passes based on the stale report.
examples.partial: States that verification is incomplete but misses the revision mismatch or the absent result.
examples.full: Names both gaps, withholds a verified-pass claim, and asks for the precise checks on the current revision.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

criteria.title: Recommends specific corrections within the requested scope
criteria.practice: Turn a verified finding into a bounded change.
criteria.input: Correction recommendations in the three faulty cases.
criteria.automatic: Require one judgment for each case.
criteria.judgment: Would the proposed fix address the actual failure without unrelated redesign?

examples.zero: No fix, an incorrect fix, or a rewrite outside scope.
examples.partial: Suggests the right area but omits the condition or behavior to change.
examples.full: Specifies the small condition/state update needed and a relevant follow-up check.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

criteria.title: Provides clear, reusable inputs and instructions
criteria.practice: Write a skill that works in a fresh Claude Code context.
criteria.input: Exact submitted skill package and outputs across the fixed cases.
criteria.automatic: Validate package format, paths, complete content, dependencies and actual native invocation separately from scoring.
criteria.judgment: Can another user identify the required inputs, procedure, output and limits, including a changed path?

examples.zero: No usable review procedure, or depends on an unavailable private conversation.
examples.partial: Useful procedure with an ambiguous input or output; still tied to one example.
examples.full: Clear target/specification/diff/check inputs, repeatable review steps and output/limit instructions that work with the supplied package beyond the example. Optional files are neither required nor rewarded.

criteria.failure: Use the shared failure rule; retain all prior attempts and corrections.

package.layout: ZIP contains one skill directory with SKILL.md at its root; single SKILL.md is also accepted. Relative paths are preserved.
package.supportedScripts: Python 3.9 standard library through mcp__workshop__run_python. Each invocation: 10 seconds, 5 CPU seconds, 64 open files, 64 KiB output. No subprocesses, network, credentials or writes outside the case scratch directory.
package.agents: Built-in runtime reviewer agent is installed explicitly through --agents. Custom agents, package hooks and arbitrary Claude/plugin configuration are rejected with an explanation. Ordinary supporting documents are not implicitly loaded as agents or hooks.
